text: The Patriots' defense absolutely suffocated the Steelers in a dominant 20-3 Week 2 victory at Gillette Stadium, with film breakdowns revealing the unit's mastery of man coverage as the standout feature of the performance, though questions lingered about whether Drake Maye had finally found the offensive rhythm that characterized last season's Super Bowl run or if the defense simply carried the load once again. The win was bittersweet on the injury front: while TreVeyon Henderson punched in a touchdown to help secure the rout, starting right guard Mike Onwenu's broken right ankle—confirmed by initial X-rays—dealt a significant blow to the offensive line's continuity heading forward. The victory marked a historic milestone for the franchise as the Patriots became the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins, a testament to sustained excellence even as the team navigates questions about offensive execution under the still-developing Maye and finds answers about depth along the interior line.
